title: Exploiting Relation-aware Attribute Representation Learning in Knowledge Graph Embedding for Numerical Reasoning

problem.claim: Numerical reasoning in knowledge graphs compares items and infers new numerical relations from relational information and numerical attributes.

gap.claim: Existing methods often rely on attribute encoders or additional loss functions and are less robust when numerical attributes are sparsely observed.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes RAKGE, a relation-aware attribute representation learning-based knowledge graph embedding method for numerical reasoning.
RAKGE learns attribute representations by leveraging associations between relations and corresponding numerical attributes.
RAKGE uses robust self-supervised learning to generate unseen positive and negative examples when numerical attributes are sparse.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluation on three real-world datasets.
The authors report improvements of up to 65.1% in Hits@1 and up to 52.6% in MRR over the best competitor.
The authors state that implementation code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Numerical reasoning supports machine learning applications and involves inferring numerical relations in knowledge graphs.
Existing approaches are often vulnerable when numerical attributes are sparsely observed.
The paper introduces RAKGE with relation-aware attribute representation learning and self-supervised example generation.
The authors report gains over state-of-the-art methods on three real-world datasets and provide implementation code.

source_observation.claim: Performance may be less robust when numerical attributes are sparsely observed.

interpretation.claim: Sparse attribute coverage is a material deployment condition for numerical reasoning systems.

application.claim: When designing numerical reasoning models, explicitly address sparse attributes through representation learning or data augmentation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these techniques generalize beyond the reported datasets or sparsity conditions.

unknowns: The identities of the three datasets are not specified.
The evaluation protocol, baseline configurations, and statistical significance are not specified.
The degree and pattern of attribute sparsity are not specified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported gains.
